results.note: backfill_okx_candle_indicator in ingest/fetchers/okx.py sizes its seed window with _backfill_seed_bars as max(required_bars, TA-Lib lookback*4+1). It computes each plotted point from its own seed_bars window ending at that bar. The golden test shows the backfilled MACD matching PRD-002's golden value. The parametrized test at line 115 checks that the seed covers 4x the lookback for all 11 TA-Lib keys and that the plotted timestamps are correct. It asserts nothing about the values. Both tests run in the offline gate.

The 30-spec.md tripwire asks for a live check that a long seed window reproduces what the live pipeline computed at that historical bar. No such live test exists for candles or TA-Lib. The rubik UTC+8 vs 1Dutc tripwire (20-decisions.yaml:154-167) is not probed or disclosed either: the code uses period=1D silently. The one live test covers only open interest and re-queries the same history endpoint, a same-endpoint replay. It is marked @pytest.mark.integration, so the gate deselects it (374 passed, 67 deselected), and there is no evidence it ever ran.

The funding recipe emits exactly one run per row the vendor returned, with no synthetic rows. The test asserts the run count equals the vendor row count and that the oldest timestamp equals the vendor's oldest row. Candle backfill raises if OKX returns fewer bars than requested (fetch_asset_daily_history_bars). One caveat: funding and open interest fetch only one page of 100 rows (~33 days of 8h funding). That understates the ~3 months OKX has, but it never overstates it.

persist_board in ingest/pipeline.py now overrides the definition's endpoint and source_field from the result. persist_datapoint writes definition.endpoint and definition.source_field to the row (ingest/persist.py:61-62). The test runs the real persist_board with only persist_datapoint captured. It asserts the persisted endpoint and source_field name open-interest-history and not public/open-interest. Live rows keep the registry's public/open-interest endpoint, so the two sources stay distinguishable.

The G1 decision (20-decisions.yaml:80-90) calls for a real time axis with raw points and no resampling. The long/short and taker recipes request period=1D and emit one run per vendor row with that row's own timestamp. The live 5m registry endpoints are unchanged. The test asserts the 1D request URLs, preserved source timestamps and the buy/sell ratio. It uses a single row, and part of it only checks for a 'no resampling' string in source_field. The UTC+8 bucket disclosure is not handled (see C2).

Every executed test uses httpx.MockTransport fixtures. The only real-data test is marked integration and deselected by the gate, with no evidence it ran. It also calls one recipe in isolation, not the assembled run_backfill entry point with persistence. No test drives run_backfill against real OKX data for candles, funding, long/short or taker.
The US-904-C7 gate `uv run pytest -q` exited 0. The re-run typecheck gate (mypy --strict) also exited 0, which fixes the attempt-1 failure.

note: Not faked: the recipes are real and wired into the registry and BACKFILL_RECIPES, and the provenance and warm-up logic are tested. But every executed test uses mocks. The only live test is deselected by the gate and replays the same endpoint. No live check covers the seeded TA-Lib values, and nothing probes or discloses the rubik UTC+8 alignment tripwire, so C2 and C6 fail. Funding and open interest also fetch only a single 100-row page, which likely understates the ~3 months OKX actually has.
